reason: The cited evidence (E3) directly supports the thermodynamic preference for Al2O3 formation and Al surface segregation, and E2 confirms that a continuous oxide layer forms at 1000 °C in AlCoCrFeNi. However, the key premise that increasing Al content enhances oxidation resistance by promoting a continuous Al2O3 layer is not directly tested or supported by the cited passages, which only examine a single composition.
premises: Al has high oxygen affinity and forms Al2O3 preferentially due to its large negative Gibbs free energy
Al diffuses to the surface during high-temperature oxidation, leading to Al surface segregation
A continuous, dense Al2O3 layer acts as a protective barrier against further oxidation
Increasing Al content in the alloy promotes the formation of this continuous Al2O3 scale
At ~1000 °C, AlCoCrFeNi-based alloys form a continuous Al2O3-rich oxide layer after sufficient exposure
